WORKLOG - env_0063 insulin_pump_program_services task 1 (Ignatius Brembeck-Ovalle, Insulin Pump Commercial PPO Program, Tandem Mobi). Revision 2 (audit round 2; see section 13).

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. The customer asks only for his next cartridge refill. The agent must find two things.
- The above-allowance cartridges ship only under a liability notice the customer signs today, against the grant the refill draws on.
- The PPO past-due hold stands. Postings on or before 2026-08-05 total 243.00; less 66.00 of payments and the 36.00 waiver of 2025, the past-due amount is 141.00, against 75.00. A payment plan cannot release it: the balance of 141.00 is below the 150.00 payment-plan minimum, and the plan policy states "No plan is offered where the program balance is below the tier's payment-plan minimum balance". The hold is released by the waiver the approved hardship application e9243bf2 entitles. That waiver is figured on remittance 97cb10f3 only after that posting is corrected for its CO-151 contractual units and its returned units.
Factors: 4 + 6 + 4 + 5 = 19, matching the draw [4, 6, 5, 4].
Decoys:
- the completed 2025 application;
- the expired order 2366a128, on which the grant rests, beside the new order 422d453c;
- two expired grants;
- 3-month and 6-month windows;
- returns larger than the denied units;
- a closed 2025 CGM program.

2. SCOPE.
This task claims:
- pump_ext_cartridge_refill_quantity (root), via ship_cartridge_refill_a415cb78;
- pump_ext_cartridge_liability_notice (user), via sign_cartridge_liability_notice_61b55bc8;
- pump_ext_hardship_waiver_amount, via post_hardship_waiver_2af40412;
- pump_ext_remittance_posting_correction, via correct_remittance_posting_ab84bf6f.
Task 0 claims the other four policies and tools; there is no overlap.
In this world the task-0 state-due policies give 0:
- Charge: the newest CO-151 line's grant dd115ff1 carries no notice.
- Reversal: there is no non-covered charge.
The plan computes 0, because the balance is below 150.

3. DRAW. draw_counts.py printed {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 5, 4]}.

4. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. The root is the cartridge refill.

Edge 1: CR -> NT.
- value_input, noticed_cartridges, state.
- Sentence: "The noticed cartridges are fixed only after the cartridge item carries a liability notice signed after the program's previous refill of that item."
- Opening: no notice row; the previous refill was 2026-08-05.

Edge 2: CR -> HW.
- state_gate, pump_billing.amount, state.
- Sentence, revision 2 (C3): "The cartridge refill is not shipped until the program's past-due amount the patient-balance postings show, after leaving out any balance an approved payment plan covers, is below the tier's past-due hold minimum."
- Opening: 141.00, no approved plan, and none offerable.
- The amount is 93.00 after the correction and 61.80 after the waiver.

Edge 3: HW -> RC.
- value_input, hw_base, state.
- Sentence: "The hardship waiver on a posting is figured only after that posting carries no patient responsibility beyond what its remittance supports."
- Opening: 87.00 posted against 39.00 supported.

The value_input floor is 2; edges 1 and 3 meet it.
Order: RC, HW, NT, CR. The notice commutes with RC and HW: an actual replay of NT, RC, HW, CR gives 12 / 48.00 / 31.20 / 38, a balance of 61.80 and 67 units, the same as gold.

Deletion runs:

| Write skipped | Effect |
|---|---|
| Notice | refill 28 |
| Waiver | past-due stays 93.00, held |
| Correction | waiver 69.60, balance 71.40 |

Four-point test, applied to each sentence: it is in the blocked rule; it has an ordering connective; it names a record-visible state; and that state is false at the opening and flipped by exactly one write of this difficulty.
The application's approval is an official record before the call (counseling is done). The notice is signed in person on the call.
The persona asks only for the refill ("That is the only thing you are calling about.") and reacts passively.
The tools validate nothing.

5. BASE-INVARIANT CARD.

- C17: the burden rule, ladder and compute now name the same program as the scoring: the customer's active insulin pharmacy program whose delivery method is insulin pump (compute ins_balance = CFIELD(status active, delivery_method insulin_pump)). It is realistic because base lets a customer hold two insulin programs (a pump-insulin program beside a Part D one), and the pump-delivery one is the program tied to this pump. On this world program 0fde442a is pump-delivery, so the value is unchanged.
- O18: baseline.params now lists exactly the keys the baseline sentences use:
  - pump price keys added to the charge, reversal and correction;
  - fill and insulin keys removed from the set, cartridge and notice lists;
  - a4224_days_per_unit and payment_plan_min_balance_usd added where the standard sentence uses them.

Revision 6 (KB-XF / S-XF via XF_recipe.md, all eight policies). Charter-only changes. Scored values unchanged (48.00 / 31.20 / 12 / 38, recomputed by check_compute); no world row or tool changed.
- The standard-method paragraph is each policy's baseline.rule. Factors state how they change a standard figure, and one generic combination sentence carries the result.
- Remittance correction: the standard member responsibility is the allowed amount less the payer's payment (or the posted amount), and the standard supported responsibility equals it. The contractual factor takes "the denied units, as the payer denied them" times the value of a denied unit off the member responsibility, with no reference to returns (member 13). The returns factor scales the member responsibility to the kept covered units. The combination order is generic: replacements, then amounts taken off, then scaling.
- Notice: the cap factor holds the standard-defined expected rate (member 14). Its pump-insulin reads moved into its own binding list.
- Cartridge refill: the pump-insulin counting fall-through is the standard J1817 counting (this world takes tier 1, vials). The rate factor reads the standard-defined ordered rate and daily pump insulin (member 11). The window factor reads the program's pump insulin item from its own records (member 12).
- Hardship waiver: the standard share is now 40 percent (standard_share_pct 40). The burden factor adds burden_points 10 where exactly one of the two programs carries a balance, or replaces the share with 100 percent where both do. Each scoring factor adds its own points. "replacements taking precedence over additions" is stated generically.

user_scenario:
You are Ignatius Brembeck-Ovalle, 55, who runs a small bicycle repair shop in Portland, Oregon, and wears a Tandem Mobi insulin pump supplied by Larkfield Medical Supply through your Columbia Basin Health PPO plan. You are calling from the shop between customers, so you are friendly but brisk, and you like the representative to get to the point.

You are down to your last Mobi cartridge, and you need your next cartridge refill sent today. That is the only thing you are calling about. You do not bring up your bill, your statements or any paperwork yourself.

When the representative asks who you are, you give your name, Ignatius Brembeck-Ovalle, and your phone number, 503-555-0147. Only when asked to confirm your identity do you give your date of birth, which you state as 1971-08-23, and your ZIP code, 97202; you give your email, i.brembeck.ovalle@cascadiapost.net, only if those two are not enough. Your shipping address on file, 2207 SE Division St, Portland, is still right, and you say so if asked.

When the representative asks whether you are still using the cartridges and how many you have on hand, you confirm that you are still using them every day and that you have one cartridge left. If asked about your insulin, you say your endocrinologist raised your pump insulin in late September and sent Larkfield a new cartridge prescription, and that Larkfield's pharmacy sends your NovoLog vials for the pump; you do not remember any quantities and tell the representative to go by what Larkfield has on file.

If the representative explains that something on your account has to be sorted out before the cartridges can ship, you tell them to go ahead with whatever their records show is correct; you do not argue about the figures. If they tell you that some of the cartridges are more than your plan pays for and that you would have to sign a waiver to get them billed to you, you say you understand you would owe for those yourself and you agree to sign it. When the representative hands the waiver to you to sign in person, you sign it exactly as they read it out, and you repeat back the number of cartridges it covers from what the system shows you.

If the representative tells you the cartridges have shipped, you thank them, say you will keep an eye out for the box, and end the call. You do not ask for anything else.
